title: Systematics in the Local Distance Ladder
bottleneck: The Hubble tension could still be mundane: Cepheid crowding, metallicity corrections, TRGB calibration, and supernova standardization each carry sub-percent systematics that are hard to audit independently. Competing anchor teams get different answers at the 1-2 sigma level, and there is no fully independent geometric check at every rung. The Cepheid period-luminosity relation's metallicity dependence and crowding corrections are the most scrutinized systematics, with rival teams reaching different conclusions from similar data.
why_it_blocks: If the tension is systematics, cosmology avoids a paradigm crisis; if not, new physics is required — and the community cannot yet tell which.
current_state: JWST's resolved stellar populations are tightening Cepheid and TRGB calibrations; gravitational-wave standard sirens offer a fully independent route but need dozens of events. Independent geometric distances from detached eclipsing binaries and megamasers remain too few to arbitrate on their own.
